item: Item 1: a how-to that the Claude session working in ~/private/xschem-private (branch assembler, HEAD a464b7f6b when read on 2026-11-21) follows to get a tip-of-the-day quiz like the one commit d36cb429e added here (engine src/startup_quiz.tcl, bank src/startup_quiz_bank.tcl, suite tests/headless/test_startup_quiz.tcl, spec doc/claude/specs/startup_quiz.md). Scout result in one line: the private tree has every dependency the engine and the suite need, 8 of the commit's 10 file patches pass `git apply --check` there, and 80 of the bank's 82 entries give the same static proof answers in both trees (the other 2 are the quiz's own entries), so the how-to can be a port-and-extend recipe rather than a rebuild.
mechanism:
ALL READ in the working tree (engine, suite and spec are byte-for-byte as committed in d36cb429e; only the bank has two reworded entries, direct-plot and calc-pick, uncommitted, for issue 1724).

WHEN. C function Tcl_AppInit (src/xinit.c), at its very end: after source_tcl_file(cli_opt_tcl_script) (--script), after the launch_library_manager autostart, after the extra-file loads, after tcleval(cli_opt_tcl_post_command) (--command) and after the `if(cli_opt_quit)` block that evals "exit %d". The hook is `if(has_x) { tcleval("if {[info commands ::startup_quiz::at_launch] ne {}} {catch {startup_quiz::at_launch}}"); }`. Earlier in Tcl_AppInit, beside the existing mirror tclsetvar("cli_opt_nolog", ...), the commit added tclsetvar("cli_opt_pipe", cli_opt_pipe ? "1" : "0") (the C int cli_opt_pipe already existed in globals.c/options.c/xschem.h).

WHAT DECIDES. startup_quiz::at_launch normalises ::startup_quiz through startup_quiz::enabled, calls startup_quiz::launch_decision under catch, stores {show reason} in the namespace variable startup_quiz::launch, and if show is 1 schedules `after $launch_delay [list startup_quiz::launch_show 0]` (launch_delay 400 ms). launch_decision builds the dict {tk automation nolog enabled questions} from startup_quiz::have_tk (info commands winfo first, then winfo exists .), startup_quiz::automation (::cli_opt_pipe), ::cli_opt_nolog and startup_quiz::enabled, and calls the PURE startup_quiz::decide, whose order is: no Tk -> {0 no-display}; automation -> {0 automation}; nolog -> {0 nolog}; switch off -> {0 off}; no eligible question -> {0 no-questions}; else {1 show}. The bank is read (startup_quiz::load_bank) only when the first four gates already say yes. startup_quiz::launch_show waits while `![winfo viewable .]` or `[grab current] ne {}`, retrying every launch_retry (200 ms) up to launch_tries (25), then calls startup_quiz::show anyway; it returns at once if .startup_quiz exists. Nothing waits on the window (no tkwait, no grab).

WHICH QUESTION. startup_quiz::show {id} -> load_bank -> startup_quiz::pick $cur -> startup_quiz::window (toplevel .startup_quiz, class Dialog, wm transient to [winfo toplevel [xschem get topwindow]], WM_DELETE_WINDOW and <Escape> -> startup_quiz::dismiss) -> startup_quiz::display. pick: pool 1 = eligible ids neither in the answered list (startup_quiz::done_ids, i.e. ::startup_quiz_done filtered to ids the bank holds) nor in the per-process `shown` list; pool 2 = eligible, not answered, not the one on display; pool 3 = a new round: ::startup_quiz_done is cut down to the ids NOT eligible in this session and every eligible id except the one on display is a candidate. Random through startup_quiz::randint (namespace variable rng is a test hook). startup_quiz::eligible evaluates an entry's `only` expression at global scope; raise or non-boolean = not eligible. Options: startup_quiz::order_options (tf fixed {0 1}; mc Fisher-Yates, an index named by `last` pinned at the bottom); startup_quiz::option_text letters mc options A..E by displayed position.

ANSWERING. A radiobutton's -command is startup_quiz::answer <pos>: startup_quiz::grade (six verdict sentences, by correct/kind/type), options relabelled "(correct)" / "(your answer)" and disabled, verdict and `why` shown, then startup_quiz::mark_done -> startup_quiz::write_done.

WHAT IS STORED, WHERE. Two Tcl files under $::USER_CONF_DIR (config.h: "~/.xschem" in both trees): `startup_quiz` holding `set startup_quiz 0|1` (startup_quiz::write_pref, called by startup_quiz::pref_changed, which is the -command of the dialog's "Don't show anymore" checkbutton, of the Help-menu checkbutton, and the body of set_enabled/toggle; pref_changed also tells the user through ::xschem::notify, caught), and `startup_quiz_done` holding `set startup_quiz_done {ids}` (write_done; written only when an answer is clicked, and NOT when startup_quiz::automation is true). Both are read back by startup_quiz::load_conf with `uplevel #0 [list source $p]` (issue 0925's shape), called from the tail of src/xschem.tcl behind an `info commands` guard, AFTER the defaults `set_ne startup_quiz 1` and `set_ne startup_quiz_done {}`.

PRECEDENCE of the switch (order of execution, read in xinit.c and xschem.tcl): --preinit, then xschemrc, then xschem.tcl's set_ne default (only if still unset), then the saved file (load_conf overrides), then --script and --command (run later, decide for that launch), then the hook reads it.

TURNING IT OFF. One Tcl variable ::startup_quiz, four doors: the dialog's box, Help > "Tip of the day at startup" (checkbutton on variable startup_quiz), the palette row help.tip_of_the_day_startup (command startup_quiz::toggle), `set startup_quiz 0` in an rc. Help > "Tip of the day (quiz)..." / palette row help.tip_of_the_day (command startup_quiz::show) asks regardless of the switch.

HEADLESS / HARNESS / SCRIPT (rows of band L measure each with a child process): --nogui: has_x is 0, the hook is never called and the bank never read (L1); xschem.tcl still sources the engine, which defines procs only (F2). --pipe with a display: {0 automation} (L5). --nolog: {0 nolog} (L7). -q: the process exits inside Tcl_AppInit before the hook (L13). --norecent: asked (L6; deliberately not a gate). A launch with only --script and a display: asked, {1 show}, window up, no grab (L2-L4), unless the script itself exits. Saved off: {0 off} (L8). --command {set startup_quiz 0}: off for that launch over a saved ON (L10). --preinit {set startup_quiz 0}: off with nothing saved, but a saved ON wins (L11, L12). Under the test harness the throwaway HOME has NO saved switch, so the default is ON there; what keeps the quiz out of every other suite is the launch flags, not the HOME: T1's hcases arm runs `--nogui --pipe -q --script`, its dcases arm `--pipe -q --logdir ... --script`, run_suites.sh `--pipe -q --nolog [--nogui] --script` (read in tests/run_regression.tcl and tests/headless/run_suites.sh). The spec (section 4) records a one-off census over a full regression run (a line appended by at_launch for that run) that found the hook reached only by this suite's own child launches.

specs_and_issues.rules: The whole design. Sec 2 what the person sees and the verdict table; sec 3 the five type/kind combinations (`upcoming` only for a feature the repository has written down as planned; a merely false statement is a `myth`); sec 4 the gates and why --norecent is not one, plus the census sentence; sec 5 the four doors and the precedence (a `set startup_quiz 1` in a PDK launcher's rc would defeat the box: do not put one there); sec 6 choice of question and when the answered list is written; sec 7.1 every question carries a proof, an upcoming one's proof says the thing is still absent, and WRONG OPTIONS ARE NOT COVERED: 'checked by hand against the source when the bank was written (a wrong option must not be a second way of doing the thing), and nothing re-checks them'; sec 7.2 the bank rules; sec 7.3 adding a question (never reuse an id; the proof must fail if the feature were removed); sec 8 file table; sec 9 not built (score, user/PDK question file, 'show me' button, answer keys).

Entry format and the P_* helper list. 'When you rename a menu entry or move a key, the proof of every question that mentions it fails; fix the question, not the proof.' 'Text inside a proof must have balanced braces.' Plain ASCII only.

States the gates, the four doors, 82 questions, and that the suite was 256 checks counted / 316 on the display arm at that commit; that src/Makefile.in obliges ./configure; that the full regression was run in a clone. It does NOT say how the questions were chosen.

Static differential of all proofs (my script, source text only): 82 entries; every P_has/P_hasre/P_order/P_file/P_sub/P_default/P_action/P_palette/P_label call, every P_proc/P_body/P_bodyre looked up as proc text in src/*.tcl, and every P_bind looked up in src/keybindings.csv gives the same answer in both trees for 80 entries; the two that differ are quiz-switch and quiz-close, which ask about the quiz itself and become true with the port. The remaining live-only fragments were checked by grep in the private tree and agree (no undo_barrier/undo_group/undo_transaction, no 'fly' in keybindings.csv/actions.csv, no sw_drag.. names, no 'combine' in wave_viewer.tcl, one -label "Calculator", no voice/recipe namespace, only ngspice registered through ase::register_backend, calc::sel_rows identical).

The ids are shared with this tree's bank, which is good for the shared answered file only while both banks hold the same ids (see family).

design_options.name: B. Engine and suite verbatim, a new bank written for the private tree

OUTLINE FOR THE HOW-TO (sections in order, with the facts each must carry)

1. What you are building, and what done looks like. One question at launch in a non-modal window; done = the suite green on both arms in that tree, a census showing no other suite's launch is asked, a full regression in a short-path clone, a look debt recorded. Point at the four source files here by absolute path and at commit d36cb429e.

2. Read these first. The spec (sections 4, 5, 7), the bank header, the suite header. State that the engine never evaluates a proof and that the P_* helpers live in the suite.

3. Before you start: re-check the dependencies, do not trust this list. A short command block the reader runs in their tree: cmp of src/action_registry.tcl, src/ciw.tcl, src/keybindings.csv, tests/banner_rule.tcl against this tree; presence of test_scratch in tests/headless/scratch.tcl; the 11-column header of src/actions.csv; the anchors in Tcl_AppInit (the cli_opt_nolog mirror, source_tcl_file(cli_opt_tcl_script), tcleval(cli_opt_tcl_post_command), the cli_opt_quit exit); the anchors in src/xschem.tcl (caught ciw.tcl source, Help menu lines in build_widgets, set_ne raw_history_max, wviewer::rawhist_load). Give the result this scout got on 2026-11-21 at a464b7f6b as dated evidence, not as a baseline.

4. Wiring, in this order, each step with its check.
 4.1 Copy src/startup_quiz.tcl and tests/headless/test_startup_quiz.tcl and doc/claude/specs/startup_quiz.md unchanged; copy src/startup_quiz_bank.tcl from this tree's working tree.
 4.2 src/Makefile.in: both files in `put /local/install_shares`. Then ./configure from the repo root, then `/usr/bin/grep -c startup_quiz.tcl src/Makefile` and the same for startup_quiz_bank.tcl, each 2. Rows F3, F4. Say that ./configure regenerates config.h, so everything recompiles.
 4.3 src/xinit.c, Tcl_AppInit: the cli_opt_pipe mirror, then the hook after the -q exit. make -C src. Rows B11, F5, F6, L1, L13. Say why --norecent / no_recent_files is the wrong thing to read.
 4.4 src/xschem.tcl, four sites: the caught source; the guarded Help entries; the two set_ne defaults; the guarded load_conf at the tail, after the defaults. Rows F1, F12, F13, Z6, E4.
 4.5 src/actions.csv: the two rows, text given exactly. Rows F7-F11.
 4.6 src/xschemrc: the commented block. Row F14.
 4.7 tests/run_regression.tcl: the entry in hcases and in dcases plus the two `##` notes; capture both arms' output first and score it with banner_complete sourced from tests/banner_rule.tcl.

5. Run it. `tests/headless/run_suites.sh --nogui test_startup_quiz`, then without --nogui. Never a bare ./src/xschem --script on the user's display: band L starts about a dozen child xschems with real windows. Which bands run on which arm; the three uppercase SKIPPED lines; that B11 needs the --pipe the drivers pass.

6. Make the bank true for THIS tree (the section that prevents false entries).
 6.1 Every A15 red is a question that is false here: fix the question (q, a, why), not the proof; if the feature is absent here, delete the entry and never reuse its id.
 6.2 An `upcoming` entry goes red the day the feature is built: move it to `shipped`, rewrite `why`, turn the proof round. Check each of the ten upcoming entries against this tree's own plans by hand once, because a proof of absence that guesses future names can stay green after the feature is built under another name.
 6.3 What no row checks: the wrong options of every multiple-choice entry and any clause of `why` the proof does not name. Review rule from the spec: a wrong option must not be a second way of doing the thing. Read all 37 option lists against this tree's menus and keys once, with the features this tree has and the other lacks in mind.
 6.4 A17 only checks that a proof calls something: whether the proof is the RIGHT check is a review question. State the standard: the proof must fail if the feature were removed or renamed.

7. Adding this tree's own questions. Entry format field by field with startup_quiz::validate's rules; the five type/kind combinations and the verdict each produces; the bank rules of band A with their thresholds; the topic cap (four topics are already at 6: CIW and action log, ASE-L, Waveform viewer, Calculator, so new ASE-L-family questions need new topic names of at most 28 characters); conventions read in the bank (right option written first and shuffled on screen, four options each, `last` for an 'any of these'); how distractors are built (a real command that does something else, with `why` saying what it does; the right label under the wrong menu; an invented name whose absence the proof asserts; a common misconception); the helper to use for each kind of claim (menu label: P_has on the exact `-label` text; palette: P_palette; key: P_bind with device, keysym code, mods, context, action id; default: P_default; subcommand: P_sub; Tcl behaviour: P_body); `only` for anything tied to a profile or a PDK, and keep at least 60 unconditional.

8. The trap for the whole tree: a startup window in other suites' runs. What gates it (--pipe, --nolog, -q, --nogui, the switch); that the throwaway HOME does not; how to repeat the census (a temporary line in at_launch appending pid, argv and the decision to a file outside HOME, one full regression in a clone, then remove the line); what to do with a hit (give that launch --pipe or -q, or `--command {set startup_quiz 0}`; never change the default). Name the one candidate this scout's static scan found there: tests/headless/test_asemc_u5.tcl relaunches xschem with `--rcfile ... --script $child` and neither --pipe nor -q.

9. Gate. Full regression from tests/ in a clone at a short path after ./configure and make; read tests/results.<pid>.log; derive the trailer delta from summarize_all's own arms (two entries, uppercase SKIPPED only), do not quote a figure from this how-to.

10. What the user sees and owes: every interactive launch is asked (the design workarea's launcher included) until the box is ticked; record a look debt for the dialog on the real screen; the two files in ~/.xschem are shared with the other program and what that means for the answered list.

11. Keeping two banks honest afterwards: a feature ported between the trees takes its reworded questions with it; the 1724 port tool's rules that say the target has no quiz need editing.

Rules for the crew that writes the how-to: cite procs and rows by name, no line numbers; every count either re-derived by a command the how-to prints or left out; file it under doc/claude/code_analysis/ or doc/claude/suggestions/, never under doc/claude/issues/.

traps: A proof covers only what its author put in it. Row A17 checks nothing more than that the proof contains a `[`. Wrong options and extra clauses in `why` are re-checked by no row (spec 7.1 says so for the options). Copying the bank into a tree with different features can therefore leave a false distractor or a false aside under a green band A. This is the gap the how-to must name most loudly.

The throwaway test HOME does not protect other suites: it has no saved switch, so the default there is ON. Only the launch flags do (--pipe, -q, --nolog, --nogui). A child launched with a display and none of them is asked. The private tree has about 70 more test suites than this one (547 test_*.tcl against 478, 207 hcases against 148, 111 dcases against 73 when counted on 2026-11-21), so this tree's census does not carry over.

The window takes no grab and nothing waits on it, so it cannot hang a suite by itself; what it can do is add a toplevel .startup_quiz about 400 ms after the hook, which changes window lists, stacking, focus and screenshots of any launch that is asked.

Without the cli_opt_pipe mirror the engine still loads and startup_quiz::automation answers 0 for everything: a --pipe session that stays open with a display would be asked, and write_done would write in automation sessions. Row B11 is the only thing that says so.

Rows F5/F6 read src/xinit.c as text: F5 takes the FIRST occurrence of `startup_quiz::at_launch` and wants it after the -q exit; F6 wants `startup_quiz::at_launch]` exactly once. A comment anywhere earlier in xinit.c that names the hook reddens them (here the mirror's comment names startup_quiz::automation and the hook's own comment names no proc).

Row Z6 wants a line that is exactly `set_ne startup_quiz 1`; row F14 wants the line `# set startup_quiz 0` exactly once in src/xschemrc; rows F9/F11 want the palette label `Toggle tip of the day at startup` word for word in three places (actions.csv, startup_quiz::hint_text, startup_quiz::pref_notice). Rewording any of them in the other tree means changing all of its copies.

src/Makefile.in obliges ./configure, and ./configure rewrites config.h, so the whole tree recompiles; in-tree the miss is invisible because XSCHEM_SHAREDIR is src/. Because the source of startup_quiz.tcl is caught, an installed tree without the files does not segfault as in issues 0423/0424: it starts with no quiz and one degraded-notice line, and a missing bank gives the decision {0 no-questions}. Silent absence is the failure mode here.

A bare `./src/xschem --script tests/headless/test_startup_quiz.tcl` on the user's display starts about a dozen child xschem windows there (band L), fails B11 if --pipe is missing, and keeps the real HOME. The armed spelling is tests/headless/run_suites.sh [--nogui] test_startup_quiz.

The suite's self-skips are uppercase `SKIPPED:`. Registering it in both lists adds two cases and no counted skip; anyone predicting the trailer from 'both lists costs a skip' will call a green run wrong. Derive from summarize_all.

Topic cap: four topics already hold 6 questions (CIW and action log, ASE-L, Waveform viewer, Calculator). One more question under any of them reddens A8. A topic name longer than 28 characters reddens A9.
An id is for ever: the answered list remembers ids, so a removed question's id must not be reused, and a question whose meaning changes should get a new id.

Proofs of absence scan file text (for example `![regexp -nocase {combine} [P_text src/wave_viewer.tcl]]`): any occurrence counts, a comment included, so an innocent word in a comment reddens the question; and a feature built under a name the proof did not guess leaves a false question green.

kind and ok must agree for true/false (validate refuses shipped with false and myth/upcoming with true), and for a multiple-choice `upcoming` every WRONG option must be something that works, because a wrong pick is told 'Not quite: that one already works.'

`only` is evaluated in the running session at global scope; one that raises or is not a boolean makes the question never asked, silently (row A18 catches it only for a plain launch). The four Cadence questions use `[namespace exists ::cadence]`, the two sky130 ones `[llength [info commands ::sky130_fet_limits]] > 0`.
